insight: Floor cleaners see a monsoon bump because of mud/dirt tracked indoors, and a second spike before major festivals when households do thorough deep-cleaning; otherwise it's a steady monthly-replenishment product.

name: Kakarla Tomato Pickle
description: Traditional Andhra-style homemade pickle prepared in small batches by SHG women, made with the named fruit/vegetable, oil and spices, sold in sealed jars/pouches.
insight: Mango and gongura pickles peak in summer harvest season; usiri (gooseberry) pickle peaks in winter (Nov-Feb) matching amla harvest. These are pantry staples eaten with rice/curd rice year-round, giving a stable base demand outside the seasonal spikes.

rawMaterials.material: Primary fruit/vegetable (mango, gongura, chilli, lemon, gooseberry, bell pepper)

name: Natural Sunni Pindi Soap
description: A natural handmade bathing soap made with a named natural ingredient (aloe vera/sunni pindi) by SHG micro-units, positioned as a chemical-free skincare alternative.
insight: Aloe-based soaps see a summer bump for their cooling properties, while Sunni Pindi soap (a traditional ubtan-style bath powder) is strongly linked to festival-day ritual bathing, especially Diwali.

rawMaterials.material: Aloe vera gel / Sunni Pindi herbal powder

name: Jute Bag Pair - Floral Print Tote Bags
description: A handwoven/hand-stitched eco-friendly carry bag made by SHG artisans, used as a reusable alternative to plastic bags for shopping, groceries and gifting.
insight: Demand spikes around festivals when SHGs supply gift/return-gift bags, and around government/eco-awareness drives promoting cloth/jute over plastic; year-round steady demand from daily shoppers as a plastic-bag substitute.

description: A dry roasted spice/lentil powder (karam podi/masala powder) mixed with hot rice and ghee - a household pantry staple across Andhra Pradesh.
insight: As a shelf-stable pantry staple, this has fairly flat year-round demand; small seasonal upticks occur when families stock up ahead of summer travel/exam season when quick no-cook meals (rice + podi) are preferred.
